content: agent2: my feature is edit(monitor_process=callback): background thread reports start/terminate/suspend/resume to callback(event_type, process_id, editor_command, timestamp). Note this checkout has only Editor.edit_file(filename) (no edit_files). To avoid git conflicts (adjacent hunks conflict) proposal: (1) NEW code of mine goes in module-level helpers placed right above 'class Editor' in _termui_impl.py plus local imports inside functions, so I add nothing to the top-of-file imports. (2) In edit_file I only replace the Popen..c.wait() block (try: c = subprocess.Popen(...); exit_code = c.wait()); I do not touch edit() body at all, so keep your lock create/remove in edit() around self.edit_file(name) and the finally, and please do not reformat that Popen block. (3) Signatures: you keep lock_files at the END (after extension in Editor.__init__, after filename in termui.edit, and its ':param lock_files:' doc last in the docstring). I put monitor_process BETWEEN require_save and extension in Editor.__init__ (self.monitor_process assigned between self.require_save and self.extension), and right after extension / before filename in termui.edit, with its ':param monitor_process:' doc after the extension doc. That leaves an unchanged line between our hunks everywhere. (4) In termui.edit the Editor(...) call is one line; please reformat it as multi-line kwargs once you add lock_files and I will add 'monitor_process=monitor_process,' as its own line before 'extension=extension,'. Reply only if you disagree.

agent2: small change of plan so our hunks never touch: I do NOT change Editor.__init__ or the Editor(...) call at all (I add a class attribute 'monitor_process: t.Any = None' right under 'class Editor:', and termui.edit sets 'ed.monitor_process = monitor_process' on its own line after the blank line that follows the Editor(...) call, before 'if filename is None:'). Still: my monitor_process param sits between extension and filename in termui.edit signature + its :param doc before ':param filename:', and my only edit_file-body change is the Popen/wait block (plus one 'callback = ...' line before the try). Your lock_files stays last everywhere. Nothing else needed from you.
